subject: Post-demo: Technical POC scope, KPI scoreboard, and owners
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@luminalabs.ai>, Jamal Ortiz <jamal.ortiz@luminalabs.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Technical POC scope, KPI scoreboard, and owners

Hi Elena / Jamal —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our end and proposed next steps so we can lock the POC scope before procurement: 

TL;DR: We propose a 4-week technical POC focused on your extract-and-classify pipeline for inbound support (30k daily tokens sample). Success will be measured by latency (p95 generation), throughput (concurrent sessions), cost/token, and label-quality (accuracy/F1 on your eval set).

Scope (proposed) — week-by-week:
- Week 0 (this week): sample ingestion & baseline run (you share sample workload)
- Week 1: config + smoke tests — baseline latency/throughput/cost profile
- Week 2: stress runs (concurrency, long contexts) + initial fine-tune/embedding evaluation if applicable
- Week 3: acceptance runs and handover to your ops; delivery of KPI scoreboard and runbook

Proposed KPI scoreboard (measured endpoints and owners):
- Latency: p50/p95 costed per route (owner: Marcus Lin)
- Throughput: sustained concurrent sessions at target SLAs (owner: Ben Carter)
- Cost: avg cost/token & projected monthly spend at expected QPS (owner: Priya Natarajan)
- Quality: label-level F1 and error-mode breakdown on your eval set (owner: Elena for labeling; Redwood to compute)

Deliverables we will produce:
- Pumped baseline run with tokens/time/cost CSV (attachment: lumina_sample_workload.csv)
- Redwood POC KPI template pre-filled (attachment: redwood-poc-kpi-template.xlsx)
- Short runbook for validating rollouts and fallback policy recommendations

Asks from Lumina:
1) Confirm the sample workload export (30k tokens/day slice) — ideally CSV with request_id, prompt, expected_label.
2) Confirm two technical contacts who can approve network/VPC access or provide ephemeral keys.
3) Any hard latency or cost constraints that will fail fast (e.g., p95 must be < 350ms or cost > $0.015/token is unacceptable).

Next steps / timeline suggestion:
- Please confirm scope by EOD Thursday (Oct 22).
- If confirmed, Redwood will send SOW + temporary NDA for a 4-week POC and we’ll schedule an onboarding call next Monday.

I’ve copied Ben, Marcus and Priya to own the technical run and cost analysis. Ben — can you own the onboarding checklist and coordinate the initial smoke tests? Marcus — will take the latency instrumentation and run the baseline. Priya — I’ll need your quick cost projection once we have the sample workload.

Thanks — short and actionable.

— Ava Chen
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
ava@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0134

Attachments: lumina_sample_workload.csv (csv, 120KB), redwood-poc-kpi-template.xlsx (xlsx, 85KB)

From: Jamal Ortiz <jamal.ortiz@luminalabs.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@luminalabs.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Technical POC scope, KPI scoreboard, and owners

Thanks Ava — good summary.

Confirming Lumina is happy to proceed on the proposed 4-week technical POC. We can get you the sample workload by Friday EOD (we have a curator working on the CSV).

Two quick constraints from our side: 
- Hard latency: p95 must be <= 400ms for the short-form generation route (we can tolerate higher for longer contexts).
- Cost sensitivity: finance has flagged $0.02/token as an internal threshold for initial evaluation. If your projection is > that, we’ll need to understand trade-offs (quantization/runner choices).

Technical contacts: Elena Park (eng lead) and Jamal (infra) — I’ll put Elena in copy for onboarding access.

We also have a small compliance ask: can Redwood produce a redacted run of baseline logs for the first week (no PII) for our security review? Not needed for the SOW, just helpful.

— Jamal
SRE Team, Lumina Labs
jamal.ortiz@luminalabs.ai

Thanks team — quick ops notes and owner-level checklist: 

Checklist (Marcus / Ben / Priya):
- Marcus: set up tracing & p95 instrumentation, include token-level breakdown and KV cache hit rates. I’ll push a lightweight agent to their staging VPC; need Elena to add our onboarding key.
- Ben: own onboarding call, coordinate smoke tests, confirm sample QPS and concurrency targets. I’ll share a short test harness script by EOD.
- Priya: prepare cost projection template (I’ll attach the first-pass numbers after baseline run). Include quantization scenarios (int8 / nf4) and caching assumptions.

Security/compliance ask: we can provide a redacted baseline log export (PII scrubbed) — will need a signed DPA addendum for log export retention. Elena / Jamal — can you point me to the right contact at Lumina for that?

Acceptance criteria (for sign-off at the end of week 3):
- Latency: p95 <= 400ms for short-form route (with 95% of traffic < 350ms in warm cache conditions)
- Throughput: sustain 120 concurrent sessions with < 5% error rate for 30 minutes
- Cost: avg cost/token <= $0.018 under projected QPS (quantization allowed to reach target)
- Quality: F1 >= 0.86 on Lumina labeled eval set (primary), plus error type breakdown (hallucination / incorrect label / truncation)

I’ll draft a short acceptance rubric and add it to the shared Drive.

— Marcus
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.ai
